name: Pinot Gris / Grigio
say: PEE-noh GREE-joh, in France PEE-noh GREE, in Germany GROW-boor-goon-der

lines.s10: Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris are one grape in two styles: light, crisp pear and lemon from Italy, rich, smoky pear from Alsace.
lines.s20: Pinot Gris and Pinot Grigio are one grape under its French and Italian names. From Italy it is light, crisp and quiet, all pear and lemon, and from Alsace it is rich and smoky, with honeyed pear.
lines.s45: Pinot Gris is a pale mutation of Pinot Noir, with a skin that is grey pink, not green. Italy calls it Pinot Grigio, picks it early and makes a light, crisp white of pear and lemon. Alsace lets it ripen and makes something else: full, smoky and honeyed, often with a little sweetness. Oregon and New Zealand tend to sit between the two, dry or off dry, with ripe pear and some weight. Pour the Italian style with light fish and salads, and the Alsace style with roast pork or mushrooms. Leave the juice on those skins for a few hours and the wine turns copper: Friuli calls it ramato.
lines.sale: Pinot Grigio is the clean slate of white wine: cold, crisp and quiet, with pear, lemon and no oak. I would pour it with the salads and the lighter fish, and keep a rich Alsace Pinot Gris for the pork.

glass.lead: Pear, lemon and green apple, light and crisp as Grigio; ripe pear, honey and smoke on a full, oily body as Alsace Gris.

ladder.where: Friuli and Alto Adige, Alsace, the Willamette Valley, New Zealand's South Island
The Veneto plain, Baden's Kaiserstuhl, Hawke's Bay and Gisborne

glass.structure: Grigio: dry, acidity medium to medium plus, alcohol medium, body light. Alsace Gris: dry to off dry, acidity low to medium, alcohol medium plus, body medium to full.

old.where: Alsace; north east Italy; Baden and the Pfalz as Grauburgunder
old.glass: Two poles. Italian Pinot Grigio tends to be pale, light and crisp: pear, lemon and a bitter almond finish. Alsace Pinot Gris is typically gold, full and oily, with honeyed pear, smoke and often some sweetness.
old.cellar: Italy picks early and ferments cold in steel. Alsace picks ripe, sometimes late, into steel or old casks; German Grauburgunder is usually dry.

new.where: Oregon's Willamette Valley, New Zealand, Australia, California
new.glass: Typically fruit forward and in between: ripe pear, apple and white peach at moderate weight. Oregon tends to be dry and unoaked, New Zealand often richer and just off dry.
new.cellar: Mostly fermented cool in steel and bottled young. The label is the cue: Gris for a riper, fuller wine, sometimes with old oak, Grigio for a lighter one.

contrast.why: Picking date decides most: early for crisp Grigio, late for rich Gris. Alsace's dry, sunny autumns let the grape hang, Italy's plains crop high for volume, and New World makers choose a style and say so on the label.
contrast.blur: Alto Adige and Friuli's hills make Pinot Grigio with real weight, some Alsace houses ferment fully dry, and a New World Gris can be as rich as Alsace.
contrast.call: Smoke, honey and oily weight lean Alsace; a neutral nose and bitter almond lean Italy; bright, clean pear at moderate weight leans New World.

service.temp: Pinot Grigio at 45 to 50 degrees Fahrenheit, 7 to 10 degrees Celsius; a rich Alsace Pinot Gris slightly warmer.
service.glass: A white wine glass; a wider bowl for a rich Alsace Gris.
service.decant: Unnecessary for either style; open it and pour.
service.age: Pinot Grigio young, within two years; Alsace Pinot Gris five years or more, late harvest wines far longer.

with.dish: Antipasti, trout or a seafood risotto
with.why: a crisp Grigio suits light, delicate plates
a cold, crisp Grigio refreshes after the mustard
Alsace Gris has the weight and the honeyed pear
the smoky Alsace style meets smoke and mushroom

labels.means: Italian and French for one grape; on a label Grigio signals light and crisp, Gris riper and fuller.
The German names: Grauburgunder signals dry, Ruländer the older, richer and often sweeter style.
The Pinot Grigio DOC of 2017 covering the Veneto, Friuli Venezia Giulia and Trentino.
Copper tinted Pinot Grigio, from a few hours on its grey pink skins.

guest.q: Are Pinot Gris and Pinot Grigio the same grape?
guest.a: Yes, in French and in Italian. The names now signal style: Grigio is usually light, crisp and dry, Gris riper, fuller and sometimes a little sweet.

guest.q: Why is this Alsace Pinot Gris sweet when my usual Pinot Grigio is dry?
guest.a: Alsace picks it much riper, and some houses leave a little sugar. Since the 2021 vintage the label must state the sweetness, so look for the word sec.

guest.q: Why does this Pinot Grigio look pink?
guest.a: The grape's skin is grey pink. A few hours on those skins tint the wine copper: a dry style called ramato, and not a rosé.

compare.tell: Pinot Blanc is lighter, plainer and fresher, with apple and no smoke; Alsace Pinot Gris is richer and oilier, with honeyed pear.
Gewürztraminer is far louder, all lychee and rose petal, with even less acidity; Alsace Pinot Gris is smoky and honeyed, not perfumed.
Unoaked Chardonnay is firmer and plainer, with no smoke or ginger; Italian Pinot Grigio is lighter still and ends on a faint bitter almond.

cards.front: Pinot Gris blind: Alsace, Italy or the New World, what tips it?
cards.back: Smoke, honey and oily weight, often with sweetness, lean Alsace. A neutral nose, crisp acidity and bitter almond lean Italy. Bright, clean pear at moderate weight leans Oregon or New Zealand.

cards.front: Grauburgunder and Ruländer: which grape, and what does each name signal?
cards.back: Both are Pinot Gris in Germany. Grauburgunder signals a dry wine; Ruländer is the older name, for a richer and often sweeter style.

cards.front: Until 2007, what was Alsace Pinot Gris called, and why did the name go?
cards.back: Tokay d'Alsace, later Tokay Pinot Gris. The name was retired by 2007 to protect Hungary's Tokaj, which is made from other grapes.

questions.q: Three glasses of the same grape are poured blind: one gold, oily, smoky and slightly sweet; one pale, neutral and crisp with a bitter almond finish; one bright with ripe pear, dry, at moderate weight. Which order of origins fits?
questions.exp: Smoke, oil and some sweetness tend to mark Alsace Pinot Gris, a neutral, crisp glass with bitter almond Italian Pinot Grigio, and clean ripe pear at moderate weight Oregon, which sits between the two.

questions.q: A guest asks for a dry German Pinot Gris. Which word on the label signals the dry style?
questions.exp: Grauburgunder is the name German growers use for dry Pinot Gris. Ruländer is the older name, for a richer and often sweeter style, and Weissburgunder is Pinot Blanc.

questions.q: A guest holds up a copper pink Pinot Grigio from Friuli and asks whether it is a rosé. What is it?
opts: Ramato: tinted by brief contact with its own skins
Rosato: blended with a little red wine
Passito: made from grapes dried before pressing
Frizzante: coloured by a second fermentation
questions.exp: Ramato is Pinot Grigio left a few hours on its grey pink skins, which tint it copper. It is not blended with red wine, and it is dry.

report: Mode contrast, as the plan fixes it. The true divide of this grape runs through the Old World itself, Alsace Gris against Italian Grigio, and the New World chooses between them by the word on the label; the entry says so in both sides, in why and in a call of three parts.
Say opens on the Court's own PEE-noh GREE-joh and adds the French and German forms.

No Codex record is believed wrong. The grid calls Friuli, Alsace and the Willamette Valley cool, so all three stand on the cool rung and the richer Alsace glass is put down to ripeness at picking, not to climate. The moderate rung (the Veneto plain, the Kaiserstuhl, the North Island of New Zealand) follows the Codex's region records and New Zealand Winegrowers.
California is named among the New World places on general knowledge and no source read in this session; a checker may strike it.
The reviewed profile gives the Alsace notes as ginger and sweet spice; the glass names gingerbread, honey and beeswax, and smoke and mushroom as Vins d'Alsace describes them.
The compare with Gewürztraminer is outside the plan's candidates and follows the reviewed profile's own confuse line. Garganega was left to its own author.
Shrimp remoulade is the one dish from the Creole table, with the crisp Italian style; no promise is made that the wine cools the spice.
The sources were read through search results; this session could not open the hosts directly.

checked.verdict: Sound after one fix. Say against GRID_SAY, the cool rung against the Court's grid read, the sweetness wording Alsace labels must carry from the 2021 vintage, the end of the name Tokay in 2007, the Delle Venezie DOC, ramato, Grauburgunder and Ruländer, and the New Zealand style were confirmed.
changed: worlds.contrast.old.cellar: German Grauburgunder is dry now reads is usually dry. The line was an absolute in a field the brief asks to hedge, and the same entry names Ruländer for the sweeter wine.
open: New Zealand: the growers' body calls its Pinot Gris nearer Alsace than Italy, ripe and oily from the North Island and tighter from the South. The entry says often richer and just off dry, which agrees; the three part call still sends a rich New Zealand wine towards Alsace, and the blur line admits it.
The copper wine takes a few hours on its skins in the entry and in the Codex's record of Friuli; sources read give four to 24 hours.
The day the name Tokay ended is given as 1 January, March and 1 April 2007 by different sources; the entry says by 2007.
California is named among the New World places with no source of its own; search lists it beside Oregon and New Zealand.
